truths.truth: /cad-plan fires the check after PLAN.md is written and before any dispatch, on the dispatched and --inline paths, refusing rather than reporting, and the refusal names each missing file beside the census it holds.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/plan.md:303 `<step name="check_census">` sits strictly between check_size (:277) and count_planned (:342), and ahead of check_gate (:374); the `--plan-time` invocation appears exactly once in the file, at :314. The step states the remedy (add each named file to that plan's `files:` list, re-run until ok:true) and the prohibition (do not continue to count_planned, do not dispatch anything, while it refuses). The inline path is covered by a pointer only - plan.md:222 names `check_census` with no second command spelling. The refusal payload observed live carries per entry `missing`, `counts` and `asserted_by` plus a hint naming the `files:` list. Both of this phase's own plans answer ok:true against the live gate.

truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/seam-calls.test.mjs is a census by this phase's own corrected D-05 - the assertion at :128 compares `seamCalls(text)` against a hand-written literal, and this phase re-pinned plan.md's row from 11 to 12 at :95 in commit 6e7fca8b. It has no registry row (`grep -n seam-calls cadence-core/bin/lib/census-registry.mjs` returns only the header prose at :47) and no CADENCE-CENSUS marker (`grep -c` returns 0), so the discovery arm at census-registry.test.mjs:138 cannot see the omission. The module header at lib/census-registry.mjs:44-49 still documents the pre-correction D-05, calling seam-calls.test.mjs the worked example of what is NOT a census and saying it "is deliberately absent from this table and owes no marker" - the opposite of CONTEXT.md D-05 as corrected. This is the very count that caught this phase's own PLAN-2 at task 6.

truths.truth: The plan-time arm fails CLOSED on a lease it could not read, the way the commit-time arm refuses an empty lease.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning/lease-check.mjs:267 `if (!atRisk.length) return ok(base);` - `censusesAtRisk([])` is always empty, so any plan parsing to zero declared paths is a PASS. Observed twice: a PLAN.md with garbage frontmatter returned `{"ok":true,...,"declared":0,"frontmatter_issues":[{"line":3,"code":"unknown-line",...}]}` exit 0, and - worse than the SUMMARY's stated case - a PLAN.md whose key is misspelled `filez:` returned `{"ok":true,...,"declared":0}` exit 0 with NO frontmatter_issues at all, so nothing on the envelope signals that the lease was never read. The commit-time arm refuses the same empty lease (planning-lease-check.test.mjs:181, `a plan whose files: list is empty is still refused as undeclared-files`), and execute.md's choose_path already treats a frontmatter_issues entry as grounds to refuse - two gates reading one signal two ways.

gaps.name: A tenth census - seam-calls.test.mjs - has no registry row and no marker
gaps.reason: missing - ROADMAP criterion 1 and CEN-01 both say EVERY hand-maintained census is registered, and one known census is not. It is invisible to the discovery arm because it also carries no marker, and the module header still documents the opposite rule.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/seam-calls.test.mjs asserts `seamCalls(text)` against a hand-written literal at :128, over rows whose `calls:` values are hand-pinned (:95 was re-pinned 11 to 12 by this phase's own commit 6e7fca8b). `grep -c CADENCE-CENSUS cadence-core/bin/seam-calls.test.mjs` returns 0, and lib/census-registry.mjs names it only in header prose at :47. That header paragraph at :44-49 still carries the pre-correction D-05 - "It is deliberately absent from this table and owes no marker" - contradicting the corrected D-05 in .planning/phases/2/CONTEXT.md:98-102. Concretely: a plan editing cadence-core/workflows/plan.md or context.md is still not refused at plan time for the count it will move, which is exactly what happened to this phase's PLAN-2 at task 6.
gaps.missing: One commit adding the row (holder cadence-core/bin/seam-calls.test.mjs; counts the per-workflow seam-invocation figures; asserted_by the generated `${row.file} instructs exactly ${row.calls} seam invocations` tests; subjects cadence-core/workflows/plan.md and cadence-core/workflows/context.md), planting the matching CADENCE-CENSUS marker at the assertion, and rewriting lib/census-registry.mjs:44-49 so the header states the corrected D-05 - row, marker and header are one act. Re-run the replay afterwards and update .planning/phases/2/census-replay.md, since a new row changes the per-entry table.

gaps.name: lease-check --plan-time passes any lease it could not read
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the plan-time gate fails OPEN on an empty or unparsed declared set, where the commit-time arm on the same file fails closed.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning/lease-check.mjs:267 `if (!atRisk.length) return ok(base);` - censusesAtRisk([]) is always empty. Probed live: a PLAN.md with a garbage frontmatter line returned `{"ok":true,"declared":0,"frontmatter_issues":[...]}` exit 0, and a PLAN.md whose key is misspelled `filez:` returned `{"ok":true,"declared":0}` exit 0 with no signal at all that the lease was never read - a case wider than the one .planning/phases/2/SUMMARY.md:48 records. Contrast planning-lease-check.test.mjs:181, where the commit-time arm refuses an empty files: list, and workflows/execute.md's choose_path, which already treats a frontmatter_issues entry as grounds to refuse.
gaps.missing: Refuse before the atRisk test when the lease is unreadable: if `issues.length` or `declared.length === 0`, emit ok:false with its own reason (an empty lease licenses nothing, which is the rule the commit-time arm already states), so a plan whose files: block never parsed cannot reach an executor on a plan-time PASS.

human_checks.name: Run /cad-plan on a phase whose PLAN under-declares a census subject and watch what the orchestrator does with the refusal
human_checks.expected: check_census emits `census-at-risk`, the orchestrator says the missing files out loud beside the census each holds, amends the plan's files: list, re-runs until ok:true, and reaches neither count_planned nor any dispatch while it refuses.
human_checks.why_human: Out of reach from here, not merely unexercised: /cad-plan is an orchestrator workflow that dispatches a cad-planner subagent and writes real PLAN files, and nothing in code stops a workflow reading prose - D-07's whole premise is this project's record of two refusals committed rather than obeyed. The seam's exit code and payload are verified; whether the workflow halts on them can only be observed in a live planning run.
